Full release notes: **https://danbyte.net/news/v0-16-0**

### New in 0.16.12

#### After upgrading (bare metal)

Settings → Updates lists these as **After upgrade** steps, each with its snippet, and hides a step once it is done. Docker installs pick all of it up from the new images.

- **nginx `/media/` block** now goes through Danbyte instead of serving the folder from disk. Until it is changed, private uploads answer 403 (the upgrade closed their folders) and images on object pages stay broken.
- **nginx `/api/backups/` block** buffers uploads and downloads instead of streaming them.
- **logrotate config** for `/var/log/danbyte`, which turns on the gunicorn log files and safe rotation.

#### Security

- **Uploaded files are served only to users who can view their object.** On installs set up with the production nginx template or Docker, `/media/` was served straight from disk, so a document's filename was enough to download it without logging in, from any tenant. Documents, image attachments and floor plans now need view on the object they belong to; branding and device-type images stay public. New documents are stored under a random folder. (#227)
- **WebSocket handshakes from other origins are refused.** The sockets authenticate by session cookie, which a browser attaches whatever page opens them, so another site could drive a logged-in user's SSH terminal or assistant once enabled. (#228)
- **A wrong password from one client no longer locks out everyone.** Behind a proxy in front of Danbyte's own nginx, every user shared the proxy's address and ten failures from anyone blocked all logins. Failures now count per client and account, with a higher per-account ceiling across all addresses. `DANBYTE_TRUSTED_PROXY_DEPTH` is documented and in the Docker env. (#226)

#### Fixed

- **A Proxmox sync no longer fails on one odd API reply.** A guest-agent answer that arrived as text instead of a list failed the whole pass with "'str' object has no attribute 'get'". Agent, config, status and resource replies now keep only the objects they should hold, an internal fault answers 500 rather than 502, and the source's sync log carries the traceback. (#232)
- **Each due check runs once.** The beat, "Check now" and an Outpost's pull could claim the same check twice, and the slower run overwrote the faster one's verdict - a down host could read "up" with its alert firing. Claims are now conditional, "Check now" leaves running checks alone, and a superseded run drops its result. (#220, #221)
- **Saved topology views save again.** Since 0.16.0 the map saves hidden cards as groups, which the server refused as "hidden must be a list (≤5000 ids)". Both shapes are accepted, a view holds up to 50,000 cards per list and 8 MB in all.
- **SSID sheets, VPN reports and keychain lists render again.** 0.16.9's credential guard refused WirelessLAN, IPSecProfile and RoutingKeychain as template subjects; they hold no secret on the row. (#219)
- **A MAC from a range you own is handed out once.** Two people with the Add MAC dialog open were offered and could both save the same address; the second is now refused with the next free one. Shared MACs outside owned ranges stay allowed. (#222)
- **Backup uploads and downloads that take longer than a minute complete.** nginx now takes the whole transfer before the web worker sees it. (#229)
- **The web tier survives a Redis restart**, web workers are capped at 8 by default so a large host no longer exhausts Postgres connections, and Redis and Postgres calls have explicit timeouts. (#230)
- **`danbyte.log` keeps every process's lines**, and the documented gunicorn log files appear. (#231)

#### Performance

- **A device's Map tab loads only the cables around it**, so its cost no longer grows with the tenant: 138 ms at 520 cables, against 493 ms before, with the same response. (#223)
- **An export template render is bounded**: refused past 50,000 rows with the count, relations joined in one query, and the editor preview over the first 200 rows. (#224)
- **An oversized XLSX import is refused as soon as it passes the row cap**, instead of after the whole sheet was read. (#225)

#### Added

- **Housekeeping.** A new card on Settings → Backups shows the stale files an install has collected and how big its backups, log, wheel and media folders are, and removes the stale ones on demand; the same pass runs every night and after every upgrade. It keeps the newest **Upgrade backups kept** before-upgrade backups and code rollback archives (default 3) and **Rotated logs kept** days of old log files (default 30). Bundle upgrades used to keep every rollback archive, pack the bundle and media folder into each one, and copy every release's wheels and build files over the last - on a long-lived bundle install that ran to many gigabytes. The first run after this upgrade clears it; `manage.py housekeeping --dry-run` shows it first.
